chunks: He said regarding the fat tails of lambs that are cut off while they are alive: Indeed, it (the cut tail) is dead (impure/carrion).

key_terms.أَلَيَات: Plural of alya — the fat tail of a sheep, a valued commodity in early Islamic culinary tradition
key_terms.الضَّأْن: Sheep/lambs (domestic ovines); the term distinguishes from goats
key_terms.مَيْتَة: Mayta — dead animal or carrion; ritually impure under Islamic law, its consumption and use is forbidden

ai.seo_question: Is a sheep's tail cut while the animal is alive considered impure (mita) in Islamic law?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that the fat tail (alya) of a lamb, when severed while the animal is still alive, is legally impure (mita/carrion). This ruling applies the principle that a body part severed from a living animal has the same legal status as carrion (mayta), regardless of the animal's continued life. This was a practical concern in early Islamic society where sheep fat-tails were commonly removed as a husbandry practice.
